title: Adley Rutschman trade grades: Did Boston overpay for All-Star catcher?
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Boston Red Sox traded for Orioles' All-Star catcher Adley Rutschman, addressing a key lineup flaw.
Red Sox gave up Carlos Narvaez and top prospects, raising concerns about overpaying for Rutschman.
Experts vary on the trade's impact, with some praising the upgrade and others citing long-term risks.

title: Here’s how much an associate professor makes in Boston
author: Annie Jonas
bullets: Retired Northeastern associate professor Jay earned $172,000 annually, living in Northborough while working in Boston.
Jay pays $4,200 monthly towards a $500,000 student loan, his biggest expense with no mortgage payments left.
In retirement, Jay will earn $18,000 annually teaching part-time at Northeastern and additional income remotely in Chicago.

title: Cambridge City Council votes to temporarily restore controversial ShotSpotter gunshot detection technology
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Cambridge City Council voted 6-3 to temporarily restore ShotSpotter gunshot detection in previously used areas.
A resident assembly will review ShotSpotter's effectiveness and community feedback, guiding future decisions on its use.
Debate persists over ShotSpotter's reliability and privacy issues, with concerns about its effectiveness in improving public safety.

title: 4 takeaways from Craig Breslow’s Red Sox trade-deadline press conference
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: The Red Sox traded prospects, including Carlos Narvaez, to acquire Adley Rutschman from the Orioles despite a steep cost.
Marcelo Mayer was traded to the Giants for reliever Erik Miller, ending Mayer's time as a potential Red Sox core player.
Franklin Arias, a 20-year-old shortstop at Triple-A Worcester, is seen as a potential future franchise shortstop for Boston.

title: ‘Playbook of destruction’: Markey, Moulton meet for combative second debate ahead of Sept. primary
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Sen. Ed Markey and Rep. Seth Moulton engaged in their second heated debate moderated by Boston 25 and GBH News on Aug. 3.
Generational change and candidates' ages were major topics, with Markey addressing concerns about his ability to serve effectively if elected.
Both candidates claimed a progressive stance while attacking each other's past war policies and campaign financing allegations.

title: 4 unproven Patriots players who are standing out at training camp
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Eli Raridon, a third-round pick, is emerging as a potential TE2 for the Patriots during training camp.
Undrafted free agent Tanner Arkin is showing potential as a strong blocker in New England's run game.
Karon Prunty and Khalil Jacobs are making strides in trying to secure depth roles in the Patriots' defense.

title: After jokes on GBH, state senator says agritourism like corn mazes are serious business
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Massachusetts farmers increasingly rely on agritourism, like corn mazes, to diversify and sustain their businesses amid financial struggles.
State Senator Jo Comerford proposed a $5 million amendment to boost agritourism and enhance cultural activities through the 'fun agenda'.
Comerford criticized GBH hosts for joking about her proposal, highlighting the economic urgency and inviting them to witness farming challenges firsthand.

title: Red Sox trade Marcelo Mayer to Giants for reliever Erik Miller
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: The Red Sox traded shortstop Marcelo Mayer to the Giants for reliever Erik Miller and minor leaguer Carlos Gutierrez.
Mayer, once a top prospect, struggled with injuries and performance, batting .223 in 114 games for Boston.
Erik Miller, a left-handed reliever, had a 2.76 ERA with the Giants this season and joins Boston's bullpen.

title: Patriots sign former Giants defensive tackle Casey Rogers
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: The Patriots signed defensive tackle Casey Rogers, formerly with the Giants' and Bills' practice squads.
Rogers played for the DC Defenders in the UFL, recording 21 tackles and 1.5 sacks last spring.
Rogers is listed as a 6-foot-4-inch, 300-pound defensive tackle, now practicing with the Patriots in Foxborough.

title: 5 things to know about new Red Sox catcher Adley Rutschman
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Red Sox acquire catcher Adley Rutschman from Orioles, sending Carlos Narvaez, prospects, and cash considerations to Baltimore.
Rutschman, 28, a former No. 1 MLB draft pick, is expected to bolster both offensive and defensive performance for Boston.
Rutschman has been injured three times this season but is recovering and could soon join the Red Sox lineup.
